articles.title: Quem são os presos em operação por suspeita de corrupção em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação de suposta cobrança de propina para favorecer processos de obras e empreendimentos imobiliários; Justiça bloqueou R$ 80 milhões em bens e valores.
articles.summary: Investigação de suposta cobrança de propina para favorecer processos de obras e empreendimentos imobiliários; Justiça bloqueou R$ 80 milhões em bens e valores.
articles.body:
Débora Alvarenga Nakanishi da Silva, Agnaldo Rael da Silva, Valdinei Monteiro da Silva, Julio Henrique Verdu Garcia e Fernando Dante Morari — Foto: Reprodução

Engenheiros civis, servidores públicos municipais e uma corretora de imóveis estão entre os alvos de uma operação que investiga um suposto esquema de corrupção em processos de obras e empreendimentos imobiliários em Sinop , a 500 km de Cuiabá. Cinco pessoas foram presas e seis servidores públicos afastados dos cargos durante a ação , deflagrada na quarta-feira (28).

Segundo o Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco), do Ministério Público de Mato Grosso (MPMT), a investigação apura suspeitas de cobrança e pagamento de propina para favorecer a tramitação de processos, a emissão de pareceres, a aprovação e regularização de projetos e a concessão de licenças e certificados. Os fatos investigados teriam ocorrido entre 2017 e 2026.

Fernando Dante Morari: engenheiro civil e servidor público municipal;

Júlio Henrique Verdu Garcia: engenheiro civil e servidor público municipal;

Valdinei Monteiro da Silva: servidor público municipal;

Agnaldo Rael da Silva: engenheiro civil;

Débora Alvarenga Nakanishi da Silva: corretora de imóveis e sócia da empresa Dnishi Empreendimentos Imobiliários Ltda.

O g1 tenta localizar a defesa dos citados.

Além das prisões, a operação cumpriu mandados de busca e apreensão contra 17 alvos. Também são investigadas possíveis interferências em fiscalizações e outros procedimentos ligados à Secretaria Municipal de Planejamento Urbano e Habitação de Sinop.

De acordo com o Gaeco, os investigadores apuram se agentes públicos e particulares teriam negociado vantagens indevidas para beneficiar processos relacionados a obras e empreendimentos imobiliários.

Entre as suspeitas estão pagamentos de propina para agilizar procedimentos, influenciar pareceres técnicos, obter a aprovação e regularização de projetos e conseguir licenças e certificados. A investigação também busca esclarecer possíveis interferências em fiscalizações municipais.

Até o momento, as informações disponíveis não detalham a participação individual de cada investigado nas supostas irregularidades.

A Justiça autorizou o bloqueio de R$ 80 milhões em bens e valores relacionados a um grupo de investigados e a uma empresa. Também foi determinado o sequestro de ativos financeiros de até R$ 3 milhões para cada um dos demais investigados, além do sequestro de imóveis vinculados a um dos alvos.

Segundo o Ministério Público, as medidas buscam preservar bens que possam estar relacionados às condutas investigadas, garantir eventual ressarcimento de prejuízos aos cofres públicos e impedir a transferência de patrimônio durante as apurações.

Os cinco presos passaram por audiência de custódia na quarta-feira (28). Conforme a decisão judicial, os pedidos apresentados pelas defesas deverão ser analisados nos autos principais, após manifestação do Ministério Público.

Os fatos investigados teriam ocorrido entre 2017 e 2026. — Foto: MPMT

articles.title: Projeto de lei propõe antecipar IPVA 2027 para dezembro em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto prevê redução das alíquotas do imposto e isenção para veículos movidos a gás natural. Proposta ainda depende de aprovação dos deputados estaduais.
articles.summary: Projeto prevê redução das alíquotas do imposto e isenção para veículos movidos a gás natural. Proposta ainda depende de aprovação dos deputados estaduais.
articles.body:
Projeto propõe antecipar IPVA 2027 para dezembro e dar desconto de 15% — Foto: Detran/Reprodução

O governo de Mato Grosso do Sul quer antecipar para dezembro deste ano o calendário de pagamento do Imposto sobre a Propriedade de Veículos Automotores (IPVA) de 2027. A proposta prevê desconto de 15% para os proprietários que quitarem o imposto à vista.

O texto foi encaminhado à Assembleia Legislativa de Mato Grosso do Sul (Alems) e ainda precisa ser aprovado pelos deputados estaduais.

Até então, o calendário de vencimentos começava em janeiro. Pela proposta, quem quiser aproveitar o desconto de 15% deverá pagar o imposto até 28 de dezembro deste ano.

O projeto de lei foi enviado à Alems nesta semana, com pedido de urgência na votação. Como o governo pretende iniciar a cobrança em dezembro, os boletos do IPVA 2027 devem começar a ser disponibilizados já em novembro.

Projeto prevê redução de alíquotas e novas isenções

O texto também estabelece de forma permanente os percentuais utilizados no cálculo do IPVA. Para carros de passeio e caminhonetes, a alíquota prevista na legislação passa de 5% para 3%. Para caminhões e ônibus, a redução é de 3% para 1,5%.

A proposta mantém a possibilidade de parcelamento do IPVA do ano em até cinco vezes. Já os contribuintes com débitos de anos anteriores poderão dividir o valor em até dez parcelas, com juros e demais acréscimos previstos em lei.

Outra mudança prevista é a isenção integral do imposto para veículos movidos a gás natural.

Todas as alterações, incluindo a antecipação do calendário de pagamento, ainda dependem da aprovação dos deputados estaduais.

articles.title: TPA Ubatuba: Câmara arquiva projeto de aumento de 80% na taxa | G1
articles.standfirst: Prefeitura retirou a proposta para reanálise e não prevê novo envio à Câmara; valores atuais da taxa continuam em vigor.
articles.summary: A Taxa de Preservação Ambiental Ubatuba manterá o valor atual após a Câmara arquivar o projeto da prefeitura que previa elevar a diária de carros para R$ 25.
articles.body:
Cidade de Ubatuba tem TPA desde 2023. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

O projeto de lei da Prefeitura de Ubatuba , no Litoral Norte de São Paulo, que previa aumentar em cerca de 80% a Taxa de Preservação Ambiental (TPA), cobrada de veículos que entram na cidade, foi arquivado pela Câmara Municipal.

Em nota, a Prefeitura informou que retirou a proposta para reanálise e que não há previsão de reenviá-la ao Legislativo neste momento. Com isso, os valores atuais da taxa permanecem em vigor, sem alteração decorrente do projeto (leia mais abaixo).

A proposta previa elevar de R$ 13,86 para R$ 25 a diária para carros de passeio. O projeto foi arquivado em 26 de outubro, segundo o sistema de tramitação legislativa da Câmara. O texto foi apresentado pela prefeita Flavia Pascoal (PL) em 25 de setembro, com pedido de tramitação em regime de urgência.

A proposta previa reajuste de aproximadamente 80,38% para todas as categorias de veículos. Nos casos de veículos de excursão, micro-ônibus, caminhões e ônibus, os valores ainda poderiam ter acréscimo da taxa municipal da Comtur, quando aplicável.

A taxa ambiental é cobrada em Ubatuba desde fevereiro de 2023 e foi instituída pela Lei Complementar nº 9, de 19 de dezembro de 2018.

De acordo com o registro disponível no site da Câmara, o projeto passou por etapas de análise da Procuradoria-Geral e das comissões de Justiça e Redação e de Finanças e Orçamento.

Em 23 de outubro, a Prefeitura respondeu à Câmara por meio do Ofício nº 668/2026. Três dias depois, em 26 de outubro, a matéria foi arquivada. O registro legislativo consultado não informa o motivo do arquivamento.

Prefeitura retira proposta para reanálise

Segundo a administração municipal, a retirada permite uma nova avaliação dos aspectos técnicos, administrativos e financeiros envolvidos na revisão da taxa.

A Prefeitura informou que uma eventual nova iniciativa dependerá de avaliação posterior, sem prazo estabelecido para o reenvio do projeto.

A administração também esclareceu que a retirada se refere exclusivamente à proposta de reajuste e não representa a suspensão ou extinção da TPA. Dessa forma, continuam valendo os valores e as regras de cobrança e isenção previstos na legislação municipal.

Prefeitura justificou reajuste por custos ambientais

Quando apresentou a proposta, a Prefeitura justificou o reajuste com base no aumento do fluxo de veículos e nos custos dos serviços ambientais durante os períodos de maior movimento turístico.

Um estudo técnico, econômico e ambiental que acompanhou o projeto apontou que Ubatuba registrou 792,6 mil veículos distintos e 1.230.878 acessos ao município entre agosto de 2025 e julho de 2026.

Segundo o levantamento, janeiro de 2026 concentrou o maior movimento, com 198.545 veículos distintos e 774.488 passagens tarifáveis.

A administração municipal também destacou os gastos com a coleta e a destinação de resíduos. Entre novembro de 2024 e outubro de 2025, foram recolhidas 59.947,63 toneladas de resíduos, com custo de R$ 30,43 milhões.

Na justificativa apresentada anteriormente, a Prefeitura informou que a atualização da taxa buscava ampliar a estrutura ambiental, com reforço na limpeza das praias durante a alta temporada, expansão dos ecopontos e fortalecimento da coleta seletiva.

articles.title: Minas Gerais tem a maior área de montanhas do Brasil, aponta IBGE | G1
articles.standfirst: Estado concentra 37,3% da área de montanhas do país. Novo mapa do relevo inclui a Serra do Curral, cartão-postal de Belo Horizonte, nessa classificação.
articles.summary: O novo mapa do relevo do IBGE revela que Minas Gerais tem a maior área de montanhas do Brasil, com 37,3% do total e a inclusão da icônica Serra do Curral.
articles.body:
Minas Gerais é o estado com maior área de montanhas do Brasil, aponta IBGE — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Minas Gerais é o estado com a maior extensão de montanhas do Brasil, concentrando 37,3% da área desse tipo de relevo no país. O dado faz parte do novo mapa do relevo brasileiro, lançado nesta quinta-feira (29) pelo Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

O levantamento apresenta, pela primeira vez, as montanhas como uma categoria própria nessa representação nacional. Antes, essas áreas apareciam agrupadas a outras formas de relevo, como os planaltos.

Depois de Minas Gerais, os estados com maior extensão de montanhas são Bahia, Rio de Janeiro e São Paulo. Entre as áreas mineiras incluídas na classificação estão a Serra do Curral, cartão-postal de Belo Horizonte, trechos da cadeia do Espinhaço e as serras do Caraça, do Gandarela e da Moeda.

O trabalho levou quatro anos e reuniu cerca de 70 pesquisadores de universidades e instituições de geologia. O objetivo foi estabelecer critérios comuns para classificar o relevo em todo o país.

Apesar da liderança nacional em extensão, as montanhas ocupam 10,2% do território mineiro. Esse percentual é diferente dos 37,3%, que representam a participação de Minas no total de áreas de montanhas do Brasil.

A maior parte do território estadual é formada por planaltos, que correspondem a 58,1% da área. As chamadas superfícies rebaixadas representam outros 29%.

As montanhas se caracterizam por apresentar um desnível de pelo menos 300 metros em relação ao terreno ao redor, além de encostas íngremes e topos angulosos.

Segundo o geógrafo Gabriel Bias Fortes, chefe da Seção de Base Territorial do IBGE em Minas Gerais, a existência de montanhas no Brasil já era reconhecida por pesquisadores. Faltava, no entanto, um sistema construído de forma colaborativa e consensual para padronizar essa classificação.

“Se a gente for pensar na estrutura de relevo, ela sempre esteve lá, ela continua da mesma forma. O que a gente padronizou foi a classificação”, explica.

O novo mapa pode servir de referência para livros didáticos, pesquisas de universidades e trabalhos de órgãos ambientais. A escala é de 1 para 1 milhão, o que significa que um centímetro no mapa corresponde a dez quilômetros no terreno.

De acordo com Bias Fortes, a padronização nacional também oferece uma base para estudos mais detalhados sobre as formas de relevo.

No Parque Estadual da Serra do Rola-Moça, a administração pretende usar o novo mapa para auxiliar no monitoramento das partes mais altas da unidade de conservação.

Segundo o gerente do parque, Henri Dubois Collet, cruzar as informações do relevo com as imagens das câmeras de monitoramento pode ajudar a identificar áreas de difícil acesso durante incêndios.

Conhecer as características do terreno permite avaliar, por exemplo, se as equipes conseguem chegar em uma caminhonete com tração nas quatro rodas ou se precisam de apoio de uma aeronave.

As informações também podem contribuir para o planejamento de trilhas. A identificação de encostas íngremes ajuda a definir trajetos e pontos que exigem mais atenção por causa do risco de quedas.

“Cruzando com o nosso sistema de câmera de videomonitoramento, a gente tem a real situação daquele relevo daqui da sala, sem precisar de ir lá”, afirma Collet.

articles.title: More than 43 million ballots cast so far in midterms early voting surge
articles.summary: Hispanic voters have helped drive the early voting numbers, which appear to outpace overall turnout for previous elections in some battleground counties.
articles.body:
With less than a week to go until the US midterm elections, which will determine which party controls Congress for the next two years, more than 43 million Americans have already voted.

Data from the University of Florida Election Lab indicates that four to five million early votes have been cast each day, representing a much higher rate than in most previous elections.

Texas has seen the highest above-average turnout rate so far, says Prof Mike McDonald, who runs the Election Lab database. Hispanic communities are also seeing a much higher turnout than usual.

Overall turnout appears on track to outpace 2020, or even 2018, which beat the 1914 record for overall turnout in a midterm election.

Texas has already surpassed its 2022 numbers by around 1.75 million voters, says McDonald. More than 5.8 million ballots have already been cast in the Lone Star state, which has emerged as a key battleground that could decide which party controls the Senate for the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.

Data from states that require voters to register a political affiliation indicates an increase is votes cast by Democrats, while Republican early voting numbers remain generally similar to 2022.

Early voting is also up among voters who chose to not register with a specific party, McDonald says, however the data does not show which candidates they chose.

Figures on Thursday show that 44% of early ballots have been cast by Democrats, and 31.2% by Republicans. A further 24.7% were attributed to voters who had no party affiliation. However, that's just for the roughly half of states that require voter affiliation.

Three states require voters to submit their race when they register - North Carolina, Georgia and Florida. Data from these states shows an increase in votes cast by Hispanic and black communities, while voting among white people is on par with 2022 early voting figures.

"That makes sense because communities of colour are more frequently part of the Democratic coalition, and whites are more frequently part of the Republican coalition," McDonald says.

Texas does not require voters to provide party affiliation or race. But the data still shows a surge in voting by some counties on the border with Mexico, which are comprised of more than 90% Hispanic people.

"When I look at those counties, what I see is some of them are going to beat their 2022 turnout in just the early vote alone," says McDonald.

Early voting has boomed in recent years, driven by the Covid pandemic when more states began offering early voting options, including both in-person and by mail.

In the 2020 election, when voters were picking both the next president as well as their lawmakers, more than two-thirds of all ballots were cast early. Half of those early votes were also cast by mail.

Voters increasingly prefer to vote in-person, even when voting early, says McDonald. They are also returning their ballots earlier than in previous elections.

He adds that he believes this could be due to concerns about postal voting, but says there is not data to indicate what could be causing this. Postal votes are more likely to be disqualified due to errors, he notes, and says some voters could be concerned about meddling in the US Postal Service.

Some officials have already confirmed records being broken. On Thursday, the city of Minneapolis said that it has set an early voting record for a non-presidential election.

Early voting will soon taper off, as states start cutting off early voting as an option in the days before the election on Tuesday, 3 November.

articles.title: Albanian opposition lawmakers disrupt parliament with smoke flares and furious attacks on socialist PM
articles.summary: Sali Berisha's microphone was cut after he declared ruling lawmakers "deserve tear gas" as Democratic Party members lit flares inside parliament.
articles.body: Opposition lawmakers in Albania disrupted a parliamentary session on Thursday by setting off flares that filled the chamber with colored smoke, marking an escalation following weeks of student-led anti-government protests. Members of the main opposition Democratic Party also blocked access to the podium during a vote on a central bank bill, Reuters reported. "These ruling lawmakers are criminals, and they deserve tear gas, rubber bullets, cracked skulls, and broken bones—not the young people," opposition leader Sali Berisha declared during a speech before his microphone was cut off. SERBIA’S STUDENT MOVEMENT TOPPLES VUCIC’S PARTY AFTER 14 YEARS, BUT POLITICAL AGENDA REMAINS UNCLEAR As the chamber devolved into chaos, fellow opposition members surrounded Berisha, holding blue flares, the official color of their party, and displaying images of protesters injured by police rubber bullets. Albania has been gripped in recent weeks by student-led demonstrations demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Edi Rama over alleged government corruption, underfunded schools, widespread unemployment, and a lack of economic opportunities. SERBIA’S LONGTIME LEADER FACES BIGGEST POLITICAL TEST AS STUDENTS MOUNT ELECTION CHALLENGE The protests began on Oct. 13 and quickly turned violent as demonstrators clashed with police and set fire to government buildings. Protesters also targeted Rama’s ruling Socialist Party headquarters in Tirana, clashing with riot police deployed to protect the property. The unrest has since spread to several other cities across the country. THOUSANDS FLOOD BRUSSELS STREETS AS ANTI-AUSTERITY PROTESTS ERUPT INTO CLASHES WITH POLICE In response, Rama, who has governed since 2013 and secured a fourth term last year, blamed "foreign hands who do not want Albania in the European Union. articles.title: A NASA wheat test on the ISS lasted 73 days: plants grew 10% taller than Earth controls, while microgravity also changed their leaves, cells, and chloroplasts
articles.summary: NASA's research on growing plants in space reveals wheat grown on the International Space Station grew 10% taller than Earth plants, with significant changes in leaf structure and cellular composition. Discover the implications for future space missions.
articles.body: Growing plants in space, under NASA’s research, has examined how zero gravity affects development from the leaf structure down to its cellular anatomy, which drives photosynthesis. According to NASA’s Station Science 101, researchers have investigated different crops and growing systems to determine how plants respond to the conditions aboard the orbiting laboratory. One such investigation aboard the International Space Station (ISS), known as PESTO, found that wheat plants grown in space turned out to be 10% taller than those on Earth. The findings are part of NASA’s wider initiative to understand whether crops can be grown during space missions of long duration. Crews may travel to the Moon or Mars, and this necessitates self-sufficient food production so they can sustain themselves during sojourns that can last for weeks, months, or years away from Earth.Wheat growth revealed changes beyond plant heightPESTO, short for Photosynthesis Experiment Systems Testing and Operations, was carried out during Expedition 4 aboard the ISS between 2001 and 2002. The wheat, identified as Triticum aestivum cultivar USU Apogee, was cultivated inside the station’s Biomass Production System (BPS) plant-growth chambers.Researchers examined gravity as one of the factors in wheat growth. On Earth, gravity provided natural directional cues for plants to grow, but in the case of a weightless environment in space, that directional reference was lost. This allowed researchers an opportunity to examine how plant structures respond and develop under microgravity.Microgravity did alter leaf development and cellular composition of the plant, but the plant as a whole remained unharmed. In addition, in zero gravity, the plant’s chloroplasts also changed; these are cellular structures where photosynthesis takes place and enable plants to convert light energy into chemical energy.Height comparison alone wasn’t enough to determine crop yield and required careful interpretation. Though the wheat grown in space was 10% taller than Earth-based plants used for comparison, it wasn't enough to verify whether a crop had more nutritional value or would produce more food. Another investigation aboard the ship, called the Seedling Growth investigation, found that seedlings were able to acclimate to the space conditions by altering the expression of certain genes related to stress. A separate investigation, Plant Gravity Sensing, examined changes in calcium levels within plant cells, which help plants detect gravity.Plant-growth systems addressed the practical challenges of spaceflightNASA uses dedicated facilities aboard the ISS to come up with solutions on how to cultivate plants in environments underpinned by crew time, water supply, and equipment. The Vegetable Production System, known as Veggie, is a low-power growing chamber that can hold six plants and includes adjustable lighting and nutrient-delivery arrangements for crop experiments.The Passive Orbital Nutrient Delivery System, or Veggie PONDS, offers another arrangement by using holders with small water reservoirs. These systems allow researchers to test methods of delivering moisture to roots in an environment where conventional watering behaves differently from watering on Earth. Another problem was identified along the way: plants not only require water but air around their roots too, and water management continued to be a technical challenge. NASA’s Plant Water Management investigation tested a hydroponic method that would supply both, while the XROOTS study examined hydroponic and aeroponic approaches to growing plants without terrestrial soil, as the other facilities also do.The Advanced Plant Habitat provided a separate facility for controlled plant research. Within its enclosed growing chamber, the colours red, blue, green and broad-spectrum white LED lighting were used. With more than 180 sensors implanted in its system, researchers monitored conditions including temperature, oxygen content and moisture around the plants. Moreover, the system could impart information to researchers at NASA’s Kennedy Space Centre, where its operation is managed, reducing the routine attention that astronauts were responsible for.NASA’s plant experiments, however, do not end here; they have also extended their studies beyond wheat. The Veg-04A and Veg-04B investigations grew Mizuna mustard, while Veg-05 examined tomatoes under different lighting conditions. Researchers compared crop yields, nutritional composition, and microbial levels with those of plants grown on Earth. Plant Habitat-04 investigated plant-microbe interactions and assessed the flavour and texture of space-grown chilli peppers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A California community searched nearly 20 years for a permanent place to gather and worship; after raising funds and beating competing offers, it completed a $16.5 million Cupertino property purchase on October 22
articles.summary: After nearly two decades of gathering in borrowed spaces, the West Valley Muslim Association has secured a permanent home in Cupertino.
articles.body: After nearly two decades of gathering in borrowed spaces, the West Valley Muslim Association has secured a permanent home in Cupertino. The organisation completed its $16.5 million purchase of the former LDS Church at 20125 Bollinger Road on October 22, 2026, closing a chapter that began when its founding congregation first began searching for a dedicated place to worship in the region. The property is a 20,761 square foot building on 2.37 acres, with 139 parking spaces, ten classrooms, an auditorium, a community hall, a commercial kitchen, and a basketball court that opens directly into the main sanctuary. According to WVMA’s Cupertino campaign page, the site is zoned BQ for religious use, meaning the organisation can use it as a mosque without seeking rezoning.A community built in rented spacesWVMA was founded to serve Saratoga, Cupertino, and West San Jose, and for decades its members have rented space for prayers, classes, and community events. The organisation described its journey as one of growing, praying, and waiting for a permanent base that could support both current families and future generations.That search lasted nearly 20 years. During that time, the community continued to operate through temporary arrangements, including the Los Gatos Islamic Center and other prayer spaces. The purchase of the Cupertino property now gives WVMA a permanent location for daily prayers, Friday prayers, Ramadan activities, youth programmes, and life events such as weddings, community meals, and funeral services, as per their website.The organisation framed the acquisition as more than a real estate transaction. In its campaign materials, WVMA described the building as “not just a masjid,” but a home for families who have been part of the community for decades and for everyone who will join in the years ahead.Why this property stood outThe former LDS Church was the first church to come to market in Cupertino or Saratoga in more than 20 years, according to WVMA. That scarcity made the listing especially significant for a community that had long sought a permanent site in the heart of the West Valley. The building was purpose-built for worship and already included much of the infrastructure a mosque community needs. Its 10 classrooms could support weekend Islamic school, after-school programmes, and adult education, while the hall and kitchen create space for gatherings, iftars, and community dinners. The basketball court is an unusual feature for a mosque and was highlighted by WVMA as a major attraction for young families.The BQ zoning was another major advantage. Religious use is permitted by right, so WVMA does not need rezoning to operate the facility as a mosque. The organisation said this narrowed the pool of potential buyers, since developers could not easily convert the property for other uses.Beating 16 competing offersThe purchase was competitive. WVMA said the property received 16 initial offers, and the association was selected as the top bidder. Its outreach to LDS leadership, a 60-day closing timeline, and a decision not to include a financial contingency helped set its offer apart.WVMA signed the purchase agreement on July 9, completed due diligence by September 7, and set October 15 as the deadline for community donations. The sale closed on October 22, meeting the timeline the organisation had laid out in its campaign.The final purchase price was $16.5 million. WVMA also identified about $500,000 in immediate work needed at the property, bringing the total immediate need to roughly $17 million, as per their website.How the community raised the moneyTo complete the purchase, WVMA set a goal of raising $10 million from the community. The organisation planned to contribute $7 million itself, while donations were intended to cover the remainder of the purchase price, immediate improvements, and early operational needs.The campaign accepted a wide range of contributions, including online card payments, checks, donor-advised fund grants, stock transfers, cryptocurrency, wire transfers, and Zelle payments. It also offered qard hasan, an interest-free community loan arrangement with a documented repayment agreement, reflecting the organisation’s stated goal of avoiding interest-based debt.WVMA said backup financing was available through Stearns Salaam Bank, but its aim was to begin with zero debt. The campaign described donations as a form of sadaqah jariyah, or ongoing charity, because the mosque would continue serving worshippers, students, and families long after the purchase was complete.A hub for the West ValleyThe Cupertino site is intended to serve Muslims across Cupertino, Saratoga, West San Jose, Sunnyvale, Santa Clara, Mountain View, and Los Altos. WVMA said the region is home to tens of thousands of Muslims who need reliable space for five daily prayers, Friday prayers, and Taraweeh during Ramadan.The property’s classrooms, auditorium, hall, kitchen, and sports facilities give the organisation room to expand beyond worship. Planned uses include youth activities, Islamic education, after-school programming, community dinners, nikah ceremonies, janazah services, and intergenerational gatherings.For a community that has spent years adapting to rented halls and temporary prayer spaces, the Cupertino purchase represents stability. The building gives WVMA a permanent address, room to grow, and a place where families can gather without worrying about leases, scheduling conflicts, or the possibility of losing their gathering space.The next chapterClosing on October 22 marks the end of a long search, but it also begins a new phase of work. WVMA will need to adapt the former church building for mosque use, complete immediate improvements, and develop programming that serves both longtime members and new families across the West Valley.The organisation said the Los Gatos Islamic Center will continue to operate, noting that the community did not outgrow Los Gatos but became large enough to need both locations. With a permanent Cupertino home now secured, WVMA has turned a nearly 20-year search into the foundation for what it hopes will become a lasting community hub.You use AI every day. articles.title: Justin and Hailey Bieber’s Manhattan condo reportedly cost $12 million; the four-bedroom residence features a 120-foot wall of windows overlooking the Hudson River
articles.summary: Justin and Hailey Bieber have added a $12 million Manhattan residence to their property portfolio, choosing a waterfront condominium in New York’s West
articles.body: Justin and Hailey Bieber have added a $12 million Manhattan residence to their property portfolio, choosing a waterfront condominium in New York’s West Village that combines distinctive architecture, expansive river views and amenities designed around privacy. The purchase was first reported by The Wall Street Journal, with further details on the residence and its design published by Architectural Digest and Elle Decor. The couple’s new home is located at 160 Leroy Street, a luxury condominium building known for its sculptural exterior and position along the Hudson River. Spanning approximately 2,800 square feet, the apartment has four bedrooms and four-and-a-half bathrooms, with a 120-foot stretch of windows that brings natural light into the living spaces while opening up views of the waterfront.Inside Justin and Hailey Bieber’s $12 million homeThe apartment’s design places considerable emphasis on light, space and the display of art. According to property details reported by The Wall Street Journal, the residence features six designated art walls, providing dedicated surfaces for paintings and other works. Scandinavian larch wood flooring adds warmth to the interiors, balancing the building’s concrete-and-glass exterior. The living and dining areas are arranged to make the most of the river-facing windows. The long expanse of glazing follows the building’s curved exterior, creating an uninterrupted visual connection with the Hudson River.The kitchen has been designed with both everyday use and entertaining in mind. Property coverage by Elle Decor and E! News describes a separate, enclosed chef’s kitchen alongside the main kitchen, offering additional cooking space without disrupting the open living area. The arrangement allows the couple to keep food preparation separate from the principal entertaining space.The primary bedroom suite also benefits from the apartment’s waterfront setting. The bathrooms feature high-end finishes, including marble surfaces and a soaking tub, while heated floors add another layer of comfort.A building shaped by modernist architectureThe condominium is part of 160 Leroy Street, a development conceived by hotelier and Studio 54 co-founder Ian Schrager and designed by the internationally renowned architecture firm Herzog & de Meuron, which won the Pritzker Architecture Prize.Completed around 2017, the 15-storey building is distinguished by its undulating concrete walls and curved glass facade. Its flowing lines reflect the influence of Brazilian modernist architect Oscar Niemeyer, whose work frequently explored sculptural forms and sweeping curves.The design also responds to the property’s waterfront location. The expansive windows give residents views of the Hudson River, while the building’s layout and private arrival facilities provide a degree of separation from the surrounding streets.Residents have access to a range of shared amenities, including a 70-foot indoor swimming pool, a wellness and fitness centre, yoga and Pilates facilities, a landscaped private courtyard and a catering kitchen. A covered porte-cochere, parking garage and 24-hour door attendant further support the development’s emphasis on convenience and discretion.Who sold the apartment to the Biebers?The seller was real estate developer Steven Brauser, chairman and chief executive of Parkland Group, an apartment development company. According to property records cited by The Wall Street Journal, Brauser acquired the condominium for $10.5 million in 2018 before listing it for $12 million in April 2026.The Biebers reportedly paid the full asking price. StreetEasy’s transaction records list the four-bedroom residence as sold for $12 million, matching the reported purchase price. The property was marketed by Adam Heller, Amanda Rosenberg and Michael Gavin of the Heller Organization, while Romy Hechinger of Compass represented the buyers.A celebrity address on the HudsonThe Biebers are not the only high-profile residents associated with 160 Leroy Street. Michael Rubin, founder and chief executive of sports-merchandising company Fanatics, owns a penthouse in the building that has been reported to be worth approximately $43 million.For Justin and Hailey, the Manhattan purchase adds a New York base to a property portfolio that includes homes in California. The acquisition also comes as the couple continues to balance their professional commitments with family life. Justin is a global music star, while Hailey founded the beauty brand Rhode, which was acquired by e.l.f. Beauty in a deal valued at $1 billion in 2025.With its Hudson River views, expansive glazing and carefully planned interiors, the West Village condominium offers a different setting from the couple’s California properties. Its combination of architectural distinction, waterfront positioning and privacy-oriented facilities makes it a notable addition to Manhattan’s luxury residential market.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: A Scottish family travelled from Florida to Britain for a holiday in 2025 but did not return; the UK Supreme Court considered whether one child should be sent back to the US
articles.summary: A family that travelled from Florida to the UK for a three-week holiday in July 2025 became embroiled in a legal dispute after the mother decided to
articles.body: A family that travelled from Florida to the UK for a three-week holiday in July 2025 became embroiled in a legal dispute after the mother decided to remain in Scotland with their two children. The father sought their return under the Hague Convention, but the mother argued that returning them could expose them to psychological harm. The UK Supreme Court ruled on 9 September 2026 that the couple’s older son, who was 14 when proceedings began, should not be sent back to the US. The court held that his wish to return to Florida was relevant, but the evidence established a grave risk of psychological harm.Why did the UK Supreme Court consider a child’s return to the USAccording to the UK Supreme Court Judgement, the father brought proceedings under the Child Abduction and Custody Act 1985, which incorporates the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction into UK domestic law. The Convention aims to secure the prompt return of children who have been wrongfully removed or retained in another country. The father argued that the children had been wrongfully retained in Scotland and asked the court to order their return to Florida.The mother opposed the application under Article 13(b) of the Hague Convention, which allows a court to refuse a return order where there is a grave risk that returning a child would expose them to physical or psychological harm or place them in an intolerable situation. The Supreme Court judgment recorded concerns raised by the mother about the family’s financial circumstances, housing instability, the children’s education and access to healthcare in Florida. She also argued that separation from her could affect the children’s psychological wellbeing and that a deterioration in her mental health posed a further risk.How did the child’s wishes influence the US return caseThe older child, identified in the judgment as H, supported his father’s application and expressed a clear wish to return to the United States. He wanted to continue his education there, in a system with which he was familiar, rather than remain in Scotland. The court considered his views as part of the proceedings, and he was separately represented throughout the case.In the earlier proceedings, Lord Braid of the Outer House of the Court of Session considered the child’s wishes alongside the other evidence. In his opinion dated 21 November 2025, he concluded that the mother had not established the Article 13(b) defence in relation to H and ordered his return to Florida. The judge considered that the child’s views were relevant to assessing whether the circumstances he would face on returning would be intolerable. The mother appealed that decision to the Inner House of the Court of Session.Why did a Scottish court refuse to return a child to the US in 2026In February 2026, the Inner House held that the lower court had erred in law by taking H’s views into account when assessing whether returning him to the United States would place him in an intolerable situation. It concluded that, without taking those views into account, the combination of circumstances he would face on returning created a grave risk under Article 13(b).The Inner House therefore allowed the mother’s appeal and refused to order H’s return to the US. It also considered whether the court should nevertheless exercise its discretion to order his return despite the risk identified. It declined to do so. The father and H subsequently appealed to the UK Supreme Court, raising questions about whether a child’s views could be considered when assessing the Article 13(b) defence and whether the lower court had been entitled to refuse a return order.Why were a child’s wishes not enough to settle the US return caseThe Supreme Court heard the appeal on 2 July 2026 and issued its judgment on 9 September 2026 under the neutral citation [2026] UKSC 32. It held that the Inner House had been wrong to conclude that H’s views were legally irrelevant when assessing whether returning him to the US would expose him to a grave risk of psychological harm or place him in an intolerable situation.The court confirmed that a child’s views can be taken into account in assessing the Article 13(b) defence. However, it also found that the child’s wish to return did not resolve the separate question of whether the circumstances he would face could expose him to serious psychological harm. His views were relevant to matters such as schooling and accommodation, but they did not address the potential harm arising from the risk that his mother might take her own life.Why did the UK Supreme Court find a risk of psychological harm to the childThe Supreme Court examined the evidence considered by the lower court, including the mother’s mental health and the potential impact on the children if her condition deteriorated. The judgment recorded that the mother had a history of depression and had attempted suicide in September 2025. Evidence from a clinical psychologist also addressed the potential psychological consequences for the children if their mother’s mental health worsened.The court concluded that the risk of psychological harm had to be assessed in light of the circumstances of the individual child. Although H had expressed a strong preference to return to Florida, the court found that his stated views did not negate the risk of serious harm if his mother’s mental health deteriorated or she died by suicide. It determined that the evidence supported the conclusion that returning him to the US would expose him to psychological harm that he could not reasonably be expected to tolerate.Why did the UK Supreme Court refuse to return the child to the USIn its conclusion, the Supreme Court held that the Article 13(b) defence had been established in relation to H. It found no basis for exercising the court’s discretion to order his return despite that defence. The court therefore dismissed the appeal and affirmed the Inner House’s decision refusing to order H’s return to the United States.The proceedings also concerned the couple’s younger son, identified as B, who was eight when the case began. The lower court had already refused to order his return to Florida after finding that the Article 13(b) defence was established in his case. No application for permission to appeal that decision was made to the Supreme Court. The final judgment therefore concerned the appeal relating to H and the legal question of how a child’s views should be considered when a court assesses the risk of psychological harm under the Hague Convention.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Cruise ships carrying were docked in Barcelona when port workers blocked terminal access over potential pay cuts, forcing some travelers to haul their luggage.
articles.body: Angry port workers in Barcelona, Spain set a barricade ablaze Wednesday, blocking access to a cruise terminal and forcing passengers to haul their luggage on foot, according to local reports. The protest took place near Barcelona's cruise terminals, where workers blocked an access road leading to the Porta d'Europa bridge, Spanish news outlet Crónica Global reported. The workers were protesting potential pay cuts, with the road closures forcing cruise passengers to walk with their luggage instead of traveling by bus or car, the same outlet reported. 'NEVER-ENDING' CRUISE GRINDS TO DEVASTATING END, STRANDING OVER 200 PASSENGERS ABROAD Roughly 200 workers took part in the protest, which lasted about four hours, Spanish outlet Metrópoli said. There was a burning barricade made of branches. Riot police were reportedly deployed to the area, according to Crónica Global. Four cruise ships carrying a combined total of more than 13,000 passengers were in port during the disruption, according to Cruise Hive. POPULAR VACATION HOT SPOTS SLAP LIMITS ON TOURIST RENTALS, DRIVING AND MORE TO PROTECT 'STUNNING' SPACES The vessels reportedly included Royal Caribbean's Odyssey of the Seas, Mein Schiff 7 and AIDAmar, which were visiting Barcelona. Norwegian Escape was also in port preparing to embark passengers for a new voyage, Cruise Hive reported. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER Spanish outlets reported that the protest followed a government audit that found discrepancies between approved salary budgets and the amounts workers were actually paid. Workers fear the findings could lead to pay cuts of up to 8%, according to local news outlet betevé. Employees have argued they should not be penalized for the discrepancies. "The solution is not to cut salaries," the workers' committee said in a statement Wednesday, translated from Spanish, according to maritime news outlet Diario del Puerto. In a statement, the Port of Barcelona said it was required to correct the payroll discrepancies identified in the government audit but maintained that the issue was not the result of wrongdoing by the port, according to local broadcaster betevé. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Barcelona is one of Europe's busiest cruise destinations, with the port recording nearly 4 million cruise passenger movements in 2025, according to the Port of Barcelona. The disruption comes as Barcelona continues to grapple with broader tensions surrounding tourism. Earlier in October, Fox News Digital reported growing tensions over tourism in Barcelona, where protests have raised concerns about the impact on visitors to the popular Spanish destination. Earlier this summer, Barcelona officials pushed to increase taxes on cruise passengers visiting the city for less than 12 hours to as much as $35, as part of broader efforts to curb overtourism. "Demonstrations and protests continue to occur in Spain. While some demonstrations have been announced, including on October 31, other protests are spontaneous. Last minute changes can happen and may occur outside planned routes," the alert said. U.S. citizens should avoid demonstrations and areas of unrest. "Stay away from areas with large crowds or significant police activity," it added. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: CBI is learnt to be probing inward remittances made by at least four foreign entities to an activist in Arunachal Pradesh in violation of the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: CBI is learnt to be probing inward remittances made by at least four foreign entities to an activist in Arunachal Pradesh in violation of the FCRA provisions.According to an FIR filed by the agency in Aug, the entities are based in the Philippines, Ireland and the UK, and CBI is likely to seek details from them regarding these transactions, sources said. It is also being investigated whether more such individuals received funds from these organisations.One of the foreign NGOs which allegedly made the transfer has been identified in the FIR as Asia Indigenous Peoples Network on Extractive Industries and Energy. Registered in Philippines’ Baguio City as a non-profit, it claims to be a regional platform for solidarity and support for indigenous communities affected by “state and corporate-sponsored extractive and energy projects implemented in their territories”. Other entities mentioned by CBI are Front Line, headquartered in Dublin, Indigenous Peoples Rights International, Philippines, and Business and Human Rights Resource Center, London.The agency has alleged that an analysis of bank account transactions revealed the activist had received Rs 20.9 lakh in the form of forex transactions. The purpose of the receipt of funds was allegedly undisclosed and the received funds were predominantly spent through UPI transactions. “Such foreign funds are being utilised to organise and sustain anti-dam protests in Arunachal Pradesh against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project and Dibang Multipurpose Hydropower Project, thereby adversely affecting economic and strategic interests of the country,” the FIR said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Mandate damages for savings lost in 'digital arrest': SC to RBI
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Convinced of bank personnel's complicity in cases of cyber fraudsters duping people by staging 'digital arrest', SC told Reserve Bank of India
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Convinced of bank personnel's complicity in cases of cyber fraudsters duping people by staging 'digital arrest', SC told Reserve Bank of India that its proposed Nov 30 standard operating procedure (SOP) must mandate every financial institution to indemnify those who lose money kept with banks to digital conmen."How do fraudsters and cybercriminals know how much money is kept in which account? Without bank employees sharing this information with fraudsters, there is no possibility of them targeting individual account holders," said a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. It said the SOP, proposed to be released by Nov 30, must mandate banks to immediately intimate an account holder when they come across a high-value transaction on the account, distinct from past transactions and inform police. It asked RBI to submit a list of banks and financial institutions to SC.Amicus curiae V S Nappinai told SC that the shared liability clause must also extend to the telecom service providers in addition to financial institutions. Noticing that most of spam calls for digital arrest are placed using WhatsApp, the bench asked the intermediary if steps can be taken to automatically end unusually long calls or devise a 'kill switch'.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bar bodies foiled plan to rope in ex-judges: Supreme Court
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With case pendency exceeding 65 lakh in high courts, Supreme Court Thursday lamented that its 2021 judgement for re-engaging retired judges as
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With case pendency exceeding 65 lakh in high courts, Supreme Court Thursday lamented that its 2021 judgement for re-engaging retired judges as ad hoc high court judges under Article 224A to speed up case disposal remained on paper, despite having been diluted, because of resistance from bar associations.Dealing with a case related to pension of judges, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the attempt to avail services of some retired judges with impeccable integrity to speed up disposal of cases in HCs has not fructified as bar associations are passing resolutions against such appointments.“Retired high court judges have established lucrative practices in Supreme Court or are enjoying better gains in conducting arbitration proceedings or in writing opinions. They are reluctant to become ad hoc judges,” said Justice Bagchi.In 2021, the apex court had activated the dormant Article 224A of Constitution and issued general guidelines for re-engagement of retired judges as ad hoc judges of HCs to help clear backlog of cases, many of them more than 15 years old. In Allahabad HC, there are more than 12 lakh cases pending.On Jan 30 last year, a bench of Justices Sanjiv Khanna, B R Gavai and Surya Kant had diluted certain tough conditions recorded in the 2021 judgment and had said a maximum of five retired HC judges could be reappointed to an HC but their number would not exceed 10% of that HC’s sanctioned judge strength.Two important conditions in the 2021 judgement that were kept in abeyance in Jan 2025 were ad hoc judges can be appointed only when there is less than 20% vacancy in an HC; and if 10% of the pending cases were more than five years old.Till 1970, some retired SC judges were reappointed as ad hoc judges in the apex court. But it was rarely the practice in HCs, with retired judges being appointed only for specific purposes – Justice Suraj Bhan to Madhya Pradesh HC in Nov 1972 for disposal of election petitions; Justice P Venugopal for two years in Madras HC in Aug 1983; and Justice O P Srivastava to Allahabad HC in 2007, as he was part of the special bench hearing Ayodhya suits.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Growing up without being able to afford Halloween costumes, Texas man Christophe Waggoner began October's Child in 2017; he has gifted 8,000 costumes to families and plans to give away 4,000 in 2026
articles.summary: Halloween is one of the most important days of the year for people across the globe.
articles.body: Halloween is one of the most important days of the year for people across the globe. Hanging up decorations, deciding on costumes and going trick-or-treating make for some of the most memorable childhood moments for kids growing up. However, not every child is blessed enough to be able to celebrate the festival fully, and many have to suffice with DIY costumes made of sheets and boxes at times.Texas man Christophe Waggoner had not been able to afford an extravagant costume for Halloween many times during his childhood, and it was one feeling he aimed to save other children from. Thus, a decade ago, he began collecting Halloween costumes for kids who couldn't afford them. Now, his Austin charity helps thousands celebrate the festivity with joy and creativity, at no cost.According to a report by Woman's World, Waggoner previously lived in an apartment where he never got visitors on Halloween. When he finally moved to his new neighbourhood in Austin, he was excited to receive trick-or-treaters. As he spent his first Halloween handing out treats, he noticed how some children arrived in simple, homemade costumes and gazed longingly at those with elaborately designed costumes. The incident made him recall his own childhood, when he did not have funds for fancy costumes. As a kid, he remembered wishing for something special to happen to make his dreams true. This is when he came up with the idea: what if all children could celebrate Halloween and wear the costume they really want?Working as a mystery shopper for resale stores, he also found himself in the perfect position to gather up some costumes to give out the following Halloween. In 2017, he officially began October's Child, where he gathered costumes year-round and hosted a costume giveaway for his community that October.Inside October's ChildFor the first five years, Waggoner stored costumes, masks and accessories purchased from resale stores and Goodwill in his garage. But as the word of his initiative spread, he had to rent a storage unit to accommodate the increasing flow of costumes donated by individuals and business partners. Soon his first storage unit filled up, and he had to rent a second, third and fourth unit.He would conduct a distribution event once a year in a church or school parking lot or apartment yard and set up tents to display the costumes. Community members would line up to check out the Halloween costumes and decorations, and pick out whatever they wanted.Over the years, Waggoner's neighbourhood project has blossomed into a lifelong passion, one which has helped him give away close to 8,000 costumes to spread the magic of Halloween among families in need.In 2026, he expects to give away more than 4,000 costumes to kids, adults, babies and even pets. The event will be held in a 7,200-square-foot area in a field next to a school, and as always, the costumes remain completely free.Keri Stern, mother of teens Mia, Izzy and Jesse, has been taking her kids to October's Child events since it started. From Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles to princess costumes, her kids have always found pieces they love. “Nobody leaves with bare bones! If someone wants to be a dragon and Christophe doesn’t have a dragon costume, he will find enough pieces to put together to make a dragon costume,” said Keri. “It’s a lot of work that he puts in. Yet at the end, he downplays how much he’s done. It’s really born out of this love he has to help.”“Seeing all the laughter, smiles, and everybody having a good time makes me emotional,” said Waggoner. “I know this is something they probably couldn’t have done otherwise. It makes me feel so good to help!”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Most of private equity in health went to west & south: Study
articles.summary: A mapping of private equity investments in India’s health sector over past 18 years has revealed investments are overwhelmingly in multispecialty
articles.body: A mapping of private equity investments in India’s health sector over past 18 years has revealed investments are overwhelmingly in multispecialty hospitals in the urbanised southern and western states, while vast rural and underserved regions attracted little or no investment at all.In the study by Brown University’s School of Public Health and Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, which identified 70 private equity (PE) backed acquisitions between Jan 2007 and May 2025, over 73% of the investment was in 45 hospital groups, including 187 multispecialty hospitals and several single ones. Among 16 outpatient care providers targeted, ophthalmology and fertility/reproductive care were the most common ones.According to the study, the investments accelerated after 2020 and peaked in 2023, which witnessed 18 deals. “This timing mirrors global post-pandemic trends, where healthcare emerged as an attractive investment sector amid favourable financial conditions. During the pandemic, low interest rates and large amounts of available capital (“dry powder”) made financing inexpensive and widely available, while healthcare’s relatively stable revenues made it more attractive than other economic sectors,” stated the study published in BMC Health Services Research, an open source journal.Karnataka recorded 13 deals, the highest number, followed by 10 each in Maharashtra and Telangana. Gujarat had six deals while Keralam and Haryana saw five each. Northern and eastern states saw minimal or no investment.Four hospital groups that together accounted for one-third of the total deals were Manipal Health Enterprises and Health Care Global Enterprises, both headquartered in Karnataka; and CARE Hospitals and ASG Eye Hospitals.Of the total number of acquisitions, 47 (67.1%) were financed solely by foreign PE firms, including those based in US, Singapore, and Mauritius, while 18 were backed exclusively by Indian investors.Among the 25 observed PE exits, secondary sales to other PE firms were most common (64%) exit strategy. Average holding period among those that exited was 5.1 years, with hospital platforms accounting for over half of these exits. Forty-five hospital groups (64.3%) remained under their original PE ownership.Several of the PE-backed platform deals were initially structured as minority stakes, with ownership expanding gradually over time, a staged pattern of engagement consistent with more cautious, multi-step investment approaches observed elsewhere in Brics markets, noted the study.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bihar Museum in world top 10, ahead of Met, Louvre
articles.summary: Artist Subodh Gupta helped put Bihar on the global art map with his signature bartan sculptures.
articles.body: Artist Subodh Gupta helped put Bihar on the global art map with his signature bartan sculptures.Even so, the art world was surprised to see the barely decade-old Bihar Museum ranked ninth on the 'World's 100 Best Museums 2026' list, ahead of institutions such as New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Louvre in Paris.Published by Munich-based travel publication Worth a Journey, the list ranks the Patna institution as No. 1 in Asia.It is the only Indian museum in the top 100. The rankings draw on visitor reviews, data analytics and on-site expert evaluations.The museum may not have the Mona Lisa, but it has a crown jewel of its own: the Didarganj Yakshi.Carved from a single block of highly polished Chunar sandstone, the 2,000-year-old, life-sized statue stands in an air-conditioned room. Her nose is chipped and her left arm broken, but she seems ready to swat away any obstacle with the fly-whisk (chauri) in her hand.Beyond the Yakshi, the 13.9-acre complex houses the famed Kurkihar bronzes, prehistoric stone tools and a Kushan-period 'Birth of the Buddha' slab. The museum building, designed by Pritzker Prize-winning Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki and Studio Opolis, an architectural practice located in Mumbai and Pune, is quite striking too.On X, industrialist Anand Mahindra called it "a seminal moment of recognition", adding that it has the potential to be a game changer for the museum-going experience in India.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: U.N. reports a sharp rise in Afghanistan poppy cultivation despite a Taliban ban
articles.summary: KABUL, Afghanistan — Poppy cultivation and opium production in Afghanistan rose sharply over the past year, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime said on Thursday, describing it as the first significant increase since the country’s Taliban rulers imposed a narcotics ban in 2022.
articles.body: KABUL, Afghanistan — Poppy cultivation and opium production in Afghanistan rose sharply over the past year, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime said on Thursday, describing it as the first significant increase since the country’s Taliban rulers imposed a narcotics ban in 2022. The agency attributed the rise to deepening poverty, which it said has driven some farmers to cultivate opium clandestinely. It called on the international community to provide support to farmers to help curb reliance on illicit crops. Afghanistan was the world’s biggest opium producer and a major source of heroin in Europe and Asia when the Taliban seized power in August 2021. They pledged to wipe out the country’s drug cultivation industry and imposed a formal ban in April 2022, dealing a heavy blow to hundreds of thousands of farmers and day laborers who relied on proceeds from the crop to survive. The U.N. agency said cultivation was up 330% and production rose by 400% compared to last year. Cultivation rose to more than 43,000 hectares (106,000 acres) in 2026 from 10,000 hectares (24,700 acres) a year earlier, it said. Farmers were concealing small poppy plots within cereal fields or inside walled compounds to evade detection, the report said. “The fourfold increase in opium poppy cultivation shows the difficulty in sustaining decreases in illicit opium cultivation when poor farmers have no alternatives to feed their families,” a statement quoted the agency’s executive director, Monica Juma, as saying. “The (Taliban authorities) and the international community need to work together to support farming communities by investing in livelihoods, farming infrastructure and access to markets,” she added. The Taliban rejected the agency’s findings, insisting that the UNODC’s report had “not accurately reflected the actual situation and has overlooked the practical achievements of the fight against narcotics.” It argued that the U.N. agency had relied on “satellite images, estimates and incorrect information from biased groups.” “In 2026, more than 26,000 hectares of land in the provinces where cultivation had taken place were cleared of narcotic-producing crops,” a statement from the Interior Ministry said. “These operations were carried out at considerable financial and human cost and under difficult field conditions,” it said. “Therefore, any assessment that fails to take these measures and their results into account in its calculations is incomplete and unfair.” The U.N. agency said that while cultivation and production remained below levels prior to the 2022 narcotics ban, the increase was the highest since the ban came into effect. The agency said that continued monitoring was required as it was too early to determine whether the increase was temporary or an indication of the resurgence in opium cultivation and production. Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi on Tuesday described the fight against narcotics as one of the Taliban administration’s greatest achievements. However, he also said the international community has a role to play to keep the drugs issue under control. “An effective fight against this phenomenon is a shared responsibility of both Afghanistan and the international community,” Muttaqi said. “It is essential alongside security measures to support alternative livelihoods for farmers, provide treatment for those struggling with addiction, and enhance regional and international cooperation against drug-trafficking networks.”
